diagnosis.what_is_wrong: The coding workload experienced severe scheduler dispatch delays beginning around 03:27:45, coincident with a newly active `python3` process consuming nearly all of an apparent ~0.25 CPU-second/second budget in the sole observed container. This is most consistent with container CPU throttling affecting `claude` and its workload threads, although the trace does not expose cgroup throttle counters, so the quota mechanism is an inference rather than directly proven.
diagnosis.evidence: Compared run_python scheduler and runtime summaries for 03:27:40.2–03:27:45.2 and 03:27:45.2–03:27:58.2: `claude` wake-to-dispatch delays changed from 17 matched wakeups (median 0.02 ms; 6 over 100 ms) to 47 (median 1,682 ms; p95 6,914 ms; 43 over 100 ms; max 7,691 ms). At the same transition, `python3` became the dominant runtime consumer, totaling 2.886 CPU-seconds in 13 seconds, while the container averaged 0.247 CPU-seconds per wall-second. The run_python event-rate comparison also showed broad scheduling/network/block event rate reductions after onset. Checked raw ctf_lines scheduler records and paired wakeups to subsequent dispatches; block request issue/complete samples were around 0.4–1.2 ms, not evidence of disk wait. ctf_proclife/procdiff found no separate service-container arrival. ctf_timeline/query_ctf returned unmatched zeros, so rates came from run_python rather than treating those query failures as absent events. The evidence supports CPU-budget contention but lacks direct cgroup throttling counters; this prevents a definitive distinction from another container-local scheduling constraint.
diagnosis.window_evidence: The onset is around 03:27:45.2: `python3` appears and begins sustained runtime, while the interval summary shows scheduler and other activity rates falling and the matched `claude` wake-to-dispatch delays worsening sharply versus 03:27:40–03:27:45.2. The observed severe-delay/collapse interval lasts through roughly 03:27:57, followed by a partial scheduler-rate rebound at 03:27:57.2; the trace tail after about 03:27:58 no longer supports extending the incident window.
